org.eclipsehealth.relay-ecg.name: ECG Beat Analysis
org.eclipsehealth.relay-ecg.tagline: Splits an ECG into individual beats and flags normal beats and ectopics.
org.eclipsehealth.relay-ecg.summary: Given an ECG recording, the module locates every beat and classifies it as normal (N), supraventricular ectopic (SVEB), ventricular ectopic (VEB) or fusion (F), then reports counts, proportions and an estimated heart rate. It ships with seven beat-classification models so you can run the same recording through different engines and see where their conclusions differ.

features.title: Beat-by-beat labels
features.text: Every beat shows four-class probabilities and a final label; abnormal beats can be filtered on their own.

features.title: Rhythm overview
features.text: Counts, proportions and beat density for N/SVEB/VEB/F at a glance.

features.title: Model comparison
features.text: Switch between or line up seven built-in models on the same input for research replication and algorithm evaluation.

features.title: Three input modes
features.text: WFDB records (with optional .atr annotations), float32 signal files, or inline samples. Single-lead input is expanded to two leads and noted in the result.

usage: Pick a record or drop in a WFDB / float32 file.
Confirm leads and sample rate, then choose a model.
Run the analysis and review the beat list, class proportions and text summary.
org.eclipsehealth.relay-ecg.goodFor: Research and teaching, reproducing public datasets, comparing classification models, skimming long recordings.
limits: Accepts 360 Hz input only; it does not silently resample.
Noisy signals, complex rhythms and paced rhythms need human review.
Output is not a diagnosis and cannot replace a clinician reading the ECG.
org.eclipsehealth.relay-ecg.techNote: Four in-house Relay-LSTM models plus three baselines, running locally via ONNX; trained and evaluated on MIT-BIH Arrhythmia.

org.eclipsehealth.relay-sleep.name: Sleep Staging
org.eclipsehealth.relay-sleep.tagline: Assigns an entire night to five sleep stages and shows the structure.
org.eclipsehealth.relay-sleep.summary: Feed in whole-night EEG features or raw 30-second windows and the module labels each window as Wake (W), N1, N2, N3 or REM, then summarises stage duration and share, awakenings and sleep efficiency. It is built for reproducing public-dataset experiments or comparing how different staging models disagree.

features.title: Five-stage output
features.text: A stage label and confidence for every 30-second window.

features.title: Structure summary
features.text: Time and share per stage, awakenings and sleep efficiency in one view.

features.title: Model comparison
features.text: Five built-in models (three in-house, two public baselines) can be compared.

features.title: Two input types
features.text: Pre-extracted 272-dimension features, or raw 30-second EEG windows.

usage: Prepare a feature .npz file or a 30-second window array.
Choose a model; in-house models use features, baseline models use raw windows.
Run staging and review window-level results plus the whole-night summary.
outputs: Counts, duration and share per stage
org.eclipsehealth.relay-sleep.goodFor: Reproducing Sleep-EDF and similar datasets, teaching sleep structure, comparing staging models.
limits: Staging only; it does not decode EDF or extract features.
Cross-dataset and cross-device generalisation has not been validated.
org.eclipsehealth.relay-sleep.techNote: Five models trained on Sleep-EDF sleep-cassette, running locally via ONNX; in-house models use frozen 272-dimension features.
